topics.title: Statics
topics.description: Analysis of forces on bodies in equilibrium — the foundation of structural engineering.
objectives: Apply the conditions of static equilibrium
Analyze trusses, frames, and machines
Compute support reactions and internal forces
Determine centroids and moments of inertia of areas

problem_templates.prompt_template: A simply supported beam of length 6 m carries a point load of 10 kN at 2 m from the left support. Find the reactions at both supports using equilibrium equations ΣFy = 0 and ΣM = 0.
Analyze a pin-jointed truss with 5 members supporting a 20 kN load at the apex. Use the method of joints to find the force (tension or compression) in each member. Draw FBDs for two joints.

A beam carries a uniformly distributed load of 5 kN/m over 4 m and a point load of 8 kN at mid-span. Find all reactions, then draw the shear force and bending moment diagrams. Locate the maximum bending moment.

topics.title: Dynamics
topics.description: Analysis of motion and forces on bodies — kinematics and kinetics of particles and rigid bodies.
objectives: Apply equations of motion to particles and rigid bodies
Use work-energy and impulse-momentum methods
Analyze planar kinematics of rigid bodies
Solve vibration problems

problem_templates.prompt_template: A 10 kg crate slides down a 30° ramp with μ_k = 0.25. Find the acceleration, the time to slide 5 m from rest, and the velocity at the bottom. Use Newton's second law in the inclined-axis frame.

A 5 kg flywheel (disk, r = 0.4 m) starts from rest and a 20 N tangential force is applied at the rim. Find angular acceleration, angular velocity after 3 s, and kinetic energy at that instant. I_disk = ½mr².

A single-degree-of-freedom mass-spring-damper system has m = 2 kg, k = 200 N/m, c = 8 N·s/m. Determine the natural frequency ωₙ, damping ratio ζ, and classify the response. Write the general solution for free vibration.

topics.title: Stress, Strain, and Material Properties
topics.description: Internal forces in materials — stress, strain, Young's modulus, and failure criteria.
objectives: Define normal stress, shear stress, and strain
Apply Hooke's law for elastic materials
Analyze axially loaded members
Interpret stress-strain diagrams

problem_templates.prompt_template: A steel rod (diameter 20 mm, E = 200 GPa, L = 1.5 m) carries an axial tensile load of 80 kN. Compute the normal stress, strain, and elongation. Is the stress below the yield strength of 250 MPa?
A stepped shaft has a 40 mm section (L₁ = 0.8 m) and a 25 mm section (L₂ = 0.6 m), both steel (E = 200 GPa), loaded by P = 50 kN. Find the stress in each segment and the total elongation.

From a stress-strain curve, identify (a) proportional limit, (b) yield point, (c) ultimate tensile strength, (d) fracture point, (e) modulus of elasticity. Explain what 'ductile' vs 'brittle' failure looks like on the curve.

topics.title: Fluid Statics
topics.description: Pressure in static fluids, buoyancy, and hydrostatic forces on surfaces.
objectives: Relate pressure variation with depth in a static fluid
Apply Archimedes' principle to buoyancy
Compute hydrostatic forces on plane surfaces
Understand pressure measurement devices

problem_templates.prompt_template: A rectangular tank is 3 m wide and 5 m long, filled with water (ρ = 1000 kg/m³) to depth 4 m. Find (a) the pressure at the bottom, (b) the total hydrostatic force on one 3 m × 4 m side wall.
A 0.1 m³ wooden block (ρ_wood = 600 kg/m³) floats in seawater (ρ_sw = 1025 kg/m³). What fraction of the block is submerged? What upward force must be applied to fully submerge it?

A trapezoidal dam face (top width 2 m, bottom width 4 m, height 5 m) holds water (ρ = 1000 kg/m³) on one side to full height. Find the total hydrostatic force and the location of the center of pressure. Use the second moment of area formula.

topics.title: Thermodynamics Fundamentals
topics.description: Energy, heat, work, and the laws of thermodynamics applied to engineering systems.
objectives: Define thermodynamic systems, state, and processes
Apply the first law to closed and open systems
State the second law and define entropy
Analyze ideal gas processes and cycles

problem_templates.prompt_template: A gas in a piston-cylinder absorbs 500 J of heat and does 200 J of work on the surroundings. Find the change in internal energy. Then identify the process on a P-V diagram.

An ideal Carnot engine operates between T_H = 600 K and T_C = 300 K. Find the thermal efficiency. If it produces 1 kW of power, find Q_H and Q_C per second. Explain why no real engine can exceed this efficiency.

1 mole of an ideal gas undergoes an isothermal expansion at T = 400 K from V₁ = 10 L to V₂ = 25 L. Compute the work done, the heat transferred, and the entropy change. Compare to an adiabatic expansion to the same final volume.
